newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - T-bonds stay upbeat, eye hurdles above 109.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bonds stay upbeat, eye hurdles above 109.

text.p: U.S. T-bond futures will retain an upbeat tone on Wednesday after a strong performance on Tuesday, technical analysts said. But they face some resistance levels above 109-00.
June T-bonds at 1014 GMT were at 108-26, down 4/32 from the prior Chicago close, having touched a 109-01 high earlier.
Raynard Cheng, technical analyst at First Chicago in London, said Tuesday had been an important day for T-bonds.
"They broke above the previous channel top at 108-18 and that has now become support," he said. "We look for the market to hold between 108-18 and 109-00 initially today."
The bias is to the upside, Cheng said placing resistance at 109-12 and above there at 109-24.

On continuation charts a 38 percent retracement of the move from a February 18 high at 114-08 to the April 11 low at 106-12, comes in at 109-12, while 109-24 is just below the March 25 spike higher at 109-25.
Tom Hobson, director of technical analysis at Merrill Lynch in London, said the market had a neutral to positive tone.

He said back-date Eurodollars, such as the March 1998 futures, reflected a better outlook for the U.S. market and he said that contract had more upside after overcoming a Fibonacci retracement level at 93.39.
That level was the 38.2 percent retracement of a fall to a 93.145 low earlier in April from a March high at 93.730.
Hobson, speaking on Reuters Financial Television, said there were trapped shorts in the market, people who had gone short of March 1998 Eurodollars some 10 to 20 basis points below current levels.
"Now the pressure is on the shorts," he said. "The market has assumed a more positive tone."
March 1998 Eurodollars were at 93.465. They surged from a 93.235 low on Tuesday.
